title: 10 ns MD of the predicted Fgf10a-Fgfr2b complex, run alongside the non-cognate Fgfr2c control
evidence_kind: SIMULATED classical MD of a PREDICTED complex; not an observation

model.name: OpenMM 8.6.1 CUDA mixed precision, amber14 + TIP3P-FB, PME 1.0 nm, HBonds, LangevinMiddle 301 K, 2 fs, 0.15 M NaCl, seed 20261102
model.context: Start: the Boltz-2 complex model (model_0.cif). Minimise, 100 ps NVT, 200 ps NPT, 10 ns production NPT, CA frames every 10 ps. One replica per complex. Nebius AI job on one H100; the job log is reassembled and checked before use.

numerical_checks.name: CA RMSD from the equilibrated start
numerical_checks.result: first 1 ns mean 1.22 A, last 2 ns mean 2.31 A, max 2.79 A; last-2-ns drift +0.15 A/ns

numerical_checks.name: inter-chain CA contacts retained (<8 A, from the start frame)
numerical_checks.result: 73% over the last 2 ns, minimum 66% of 95 initial pairs; the two chains never separate (closest CA 4.4 A at the end)

numerical_checks.name: SAME RUN ON THE NON-COGNATE IIIc CONTROL: contacts retained
numerical_checks.result: 62% over the last 2 ns (minimum 56%) of 68 initial pairs; CA RMSD last 2 ns 1.64 A

numerical_checks.name: what the control implies for MD as a specificity test
numerical_checks.result: the non-cognate interface stays within the same range as the cognate one over 10 ns (62% vs 73% retained, from 68 vs 95 initial pairs), so interface persistence at this length does NOT discriminate the isoforms; the only difference is how many contacts the prediction started with

numerical_checks.name: the same comparison as an absolute count, not a fraction
numerical_checks.result: 69.5 surviving inter-chain CA pairs for the cognate complex vs 42.4 for the non-cognate (1.64x). Reported as a fraction the two look similar (73 % vs 62 %); as an absolute count they do not (69.5 vs 42.4 surviving pairs, 1.64x). Both are stated. The count gap is inherited from the predicted starting poses (95 vs 68 initial pairs), not produced by the MD, and the predictor scored the NON-cognate complex higher, so the gap cannot be read as isoform specificity without a template-free prediction to compare against.

numerical_checks.name: per-residue flexibility vs start-model pLDDT, pooled over both chains
numerical_checks.result: Spearman rho -0.10 (p=0.053): not significant pooled - but see the per-chain correction below, which is where this test belongs

numerical_checks.name: radius of gyration, first vs last frame
CORRECTION: flexibility vs confidence, split by chain instead of pooled
numerical_checks.result: cognate_fgf10a_fgfr2b | chain A, interface residues: rho -0.697 (R2 0.486, n=37); noncognate_fgf10a_fgfr2c | chain A, interface residues: rho -0.703 (R2 0.495, n=36). 14 groups tested, Bonferroni alpha 0.00357. The pooled test was the wrong test. Splitting by chain, the anticorrelation between per-residue flexibility and start-model pLDDT is concentrated in the LIGAND chain's INTERFACE residues and is strong there in BOTH complexes independently (cognate rho -0.70, non-cognate rho -0.70, R2 ~0.49, p ~2e-6, surviving Bonferroni). The receptor chain shows nothing. So the earlier 'the correlation does not reproduce on the complex' was a dilution artefact: the receptor chain is built from a close template, scores uniformly high pLDDT and contributes little rank spread, which flattens the pooled statistic. The earlier null is withdrawn and replaced by this narrower, reproduced result.

parameter_unknowns: Force-field and water-model error are not quantified.
No ddG was computed: the hosted stab_ddg tool needs an upload manifest whose format is undocumented.
open_questions: Do the two complexes separate over hundreds of ns, or under free-energy perturbation?
limitations: Single replica per complex, 10 ns: too short for a binding claim.
Both starts are predictions, and the predictor already failed its isoform control.
does_not_establish: binding affinity, ddG or on/off rates
FGF10-FGFR2b isoform specificity: the non-cognate control behaves the same way
that the predicted docking pose is correct (a wrong pose can also persist for 10 ns)
a causal link between predictor confidence and simulated flexibility: both may follow from the same sparse MSA coverage
that the flexibility is local - whole-complex superposition leaves rigid-body rocking in the RMSF
anything about fin size or flight
